messages:
maria: Heads up — we started seeing ~30k 'silent' SSE connections in prod over the last hour. Socket stays ESTABLISHED, no events for ~40–90s, clients don't reconnect, console shows no errors.
kevin: Hmm. Are those across regions or a single edge?
maria: Mostly us-east-1, small tail in eu-west. Traffic spike around 12:04 UTC.
jen: Does the runtime emit any pingback/last-seen telemetry? The console only surfaces last successful frame timestamps today.
maria: Logs show normal pings from the LB, no application-level events. Sample log:
```
2026-03-20T12:04:12Z connection_id=abc123 edge=us-east-1 state=ESTABLISHED last_app_event=2026-03-20T12:03:35Z
2026-03-20T12:05:00Z no_app_frames_since=85s
```
ida: Could be client-side stall (browser tab throttling) vs server-side pause. Any correlation with CPU/GPU spikes on serving hosts?
raul: Checked node stats — CPU and network look normal. No eviction or OOM. We do have a new rollout of a tiny middleware in the routing plane at 12:00, maybe it altered keepalive semantics.
kevin: The middleware briefly toggled `tcp_keepalive` to 300s for a config test. That would increase OS-level keepalive; clients might not detect silent streams.
jen: That explains clients not reconnecting. But we still need visibility and a mitigation. Two problems: (1) silent sockets inflate active connection count (billing/quotas), (2) UX — console shows healthy.
maria: Proposal: add an app-level idle_timeout separate from TCP keepalive — after N seconds without app frames, mark connection as "idle" and emit telemetry + optional server-side soft-close.
ida: +1. Also add a console widget: idle_rate, avg-idle-duration, percent of active connections that are app-idle. Right now ops sees only socket count and last_event_histo.
raul: Implementation note: cannot unilaterally close for all cost tiers. For Hosted tier we can soft-close after 60s, for Dedicated customers need opt-in or config flag. Private deployments should get a toggle.
kevin: Could we do a graceful-close that sends a JSON end-event so clients know to reconnect and we don't charge duplicate tokens on reconnect? Something like: `event: server_idle
data: {"reason":"idle_close","suggest_reconnect":true}`
maria: Yes, send a final event then close connection. Also set a reconnect-backoff header so clients don't hammer.
jen: On console/alerting side, add an alert rule: sudden rise in app-idle > 5% over baseline within 5m. And instrument rollouts so config flips (like keepalive change) get tagged in the telemetry UI.
ida: We should also add an A/B experiment: rollout app-idle-close to small percentage and track 'reconnect churn' and 'duplicate billing markers' metrics.
raul: Agree. For quota accounting: mark tokens consumed up to server-close, and if client reconnects within short window, attribute to same session id to avoid double-billing. Needs console docs.
kevin: Implementation plan estimate: runtime change + router header + console telemetry + rollout flags => 2 sprints (runtime + one sprint for console). Is that acceptable?
maria: Let's triage: short-term patch — revert keepalive toggle and enable app-idle telemetry only. Mid-term — idle-close + console + rollout. Docs/SDK: add recommended client behavior to reconnect on server_idle and honor `Reconnect-After` header.
jen: I'll add a console ticket for widgets + alerting. Can product own the rollout gating policy for enterprise tiers?
raul: Yes, I'll coordinate with product. Also add automated regression tests simulating browser throttling and long polling edgecases.
ops-bot: Incident created: #INC-2026-101. Pager duty notified.
maria: Thanks — I'll open the runtime PR for telemetry streaming today and ping for reviews. If anyone can help validate on a canary (us-east small cluster) after the revert, that would be great. :thumbsup:
